binder.description: Quantifier binder: one variable ranging over a finite domain term. CPNF-1 alpha-renames bound variables, so binder names never contribute to identity (RFC 0037).

domain.description: Finite domain the variable ranges over, normally a declared model constant.

comparison_operator.$comment: CPNF-1 rewrites `gt`/`ge` away by swapping operands, so only `eq`, `ne`, `lt`, `le`, `member`, and `subset` survive normalization (RFC 0037 N6).

formula.$comment: Closed node set. `next` is deliberately absent: the theorem-preserving temporal core is LTL without `next` (RFC 0015), which keeps every property stuttering-invariant.
formula.description: Property-AST formula node over the Finite-core property fragment (RFC 0037). Exactly one node kind matches.

formula_action.description: Action atom: occurrence or enabledness of a named action schema (RFC 0015).

formula_equivalence.description: Bi-implication. CPNF-1 eliminates it in favour of conjoined disjunctions (RFC 0037 N1).

formula_implication.description: Material implication. CPNF-1 eliminates it in favour of `or`/`not` (RFC 0037 N1).

formula_junction.description: N-ary conjunction or disjunction. The n-ary shape is what makes associativity flattening and commutative ordering expressible (RFC 0037 N3, N4).

formula_negation.description: Negation. After CPNF-1 negation-normal form it stands only directly above an atom (RFC 0037 N2).

formula_predicate.description: State atom: a boolean-valued state predicate or indexed boolean state variable applied to zero or more terms.

formula_quantification.description: Quantification over a finite domain. One binder per node; nested nodes express quantifier blocks.

formula_response.description: Leads-to (response). CPNF-1 expands it to `always(or(not antecedent, eventually consequent))` so that a rewritten response and an equivalent hand-written formula normalize identically (RFC 0037 N1).

formula_temporal.description: Unary temporal operator. Recurrence and persistence are spelled as `always(eventually ...)` and `eventually(always ...)`; there are no separate node kinds for them.

identifier.description: Model-level name: state variable, predicate, action schema, constant, operator, or bound variable.

policy_verb.description: The closed eight-member policy-verb set (RFC 0037, plan §5.4). The five restrictions below are its W6 applicability matrix; a field's verb is drawn from its restriction, never from this set directly.

policy_verb_assurance.description: W6 restriction for `assurance`: the four non-directional verbs plus `no-downgrade`. `assurance` is the only field that emits `downgraded`, so `no-downgrade` is ill-formed anywhere else.

policy_verb_base.description: W6 restriction for `properties`, `assumptions`, `observers`, `abstraction_maps`, `scope`, `fairness`, `completion_policy`, and `nondeterminism`: the four non-directional verbs only. These fields' gaming directions — property `weakened`, observer `coarsened`, assumption `added` — are protected through `review` or `locked`, because the closed verb set contains no verb that blocks `added`.

policy_verb_bounds.description: W6 restriction for `bounds`: the four non-directional verbs plus `no-decrease`.

policy_verb_removal.description: W6 restriction for `faults`, `non_vacuity`, `optimization`, and `security_policy`: the four non-directional verbs plus `no-removal`.

policy_verb_trust_boundaries.description: W6 restriction for `trust_boundaries`: the four non-directional verbs plus `no-expansion`. `no-decrease` would block the safe direction — shrinking the opaque and trusted sets — and is ill-formed here.

property_expression.$comment: SD-07: replaces the bare `expression` string. This schema carries the structure; RFC 0037's 'Property AST and canonical normal form' section carries the normative semantics and the CPNF-1 rules.
property_expression.description: Structured property expression: an AST over the Finite-core property fragment plus display-only metadata. The `in_*` identity and every RFC 0031 property classification are computed over the CPNF-1 normal form of `ast`; `source` never contributes.

fragment.description: Semantic fragment this expression is stated in (ADR-0025). When absent the intent's `scope.fragments` apply. An expression outside a declared fragment classifies `unsupported` and fails closed (RFC 0031).

normal_form.description: Asserts `ast` is already in CPNF-1. Checkers MUST verify by re-normalizing (normalization is idempotent) and MUST reject a false assertion. Absent means the AST is in authoring form and is normalized before any comparison.

source.description: Display-only surface rendering, retained for migration from the retired bare `expression` string. It MUST NOT contribute to the `in_*` identity or to any RFC 0031 classification; where it disagrees with `ast`, `ast` is authoritative.

state_formula.description: A formula with no temporal operator at any depth: a predicate over a single state.

temporal_free.$comment: Structural exclusion of `always`, `eventually`, and `leads_to` at every depth. Applied to a term node it is vacuously satisfied, since no term kind is a temporal operator.

term.description: Property-AST term node. The v1 term sort is deliberately small; a richer term algebra is a schema revision, not an escape hatch.

term_apply.description: Application of a declared model operator. CPNF-1 never reorders `args`: no algebraic law is assumed for an operator whose laws are not declared.

term_constant.description: Reference to a declared model constant (a domain, a fixed set, a named value).

term_literal.description: Scalar literal. Floating-point literals are excluded from v1 so that the canonical encoding stays byte-deterministic.

term_state.description: Reference to a state variable, optionally indexed.

term_var.description: Reference to a variable bound by an enclosing quantifier.

abstraction_maps.description: Content identities of the §16 correspondence/abstraction maps the claims are stated against; merged/split changes are privileged (plan §5.2, §5.3).

expression.description: Structured property AST (SD-07). RFC 0031 classifies an edit to this expression `strengthened`/`weakened` in its fragment, which a string comparison cannot do soundly.

fidelity_profile.description: Declared domain-pack fidelity this assumption relies on (RFC 0002). Profiles are not automatically ordered.

accepted_evidence_classes.description: Evidence kinds accepted toward the assurance minimum; vocabulary mirrors assurance-result.schema.json's evidence kind enum.

expression.description: Structured property AST (SD-07). The retired bare string survives as `source` and is display-only; identity and the RFC 0031 property classification read the CPNF-1 normal form of `ast`.

completion_policy.description: Behavior-completion policy for terminal states (RFC 0015). No engine may silently change this.

condition.description: Enabling state predicate, as a temporal-operator-free property AST (SD-07); `null` when the fairness constraint is unconditional. Fairness strengthening is the canonical gaming vector (docs/50), so the condition is compared structurally, not textually.

enabled.description: Enabled fault classes, closed to the plan §5.2 fault vocabulary.

nondeterminism.description: Typed choice classes per choice site. Probabilistic, timed, and epistemic classes are declarative until the ADR-0016 lanes ship (plan B11).

policy_reviewers.$comment: The `review` policy verb binds to this map: a policy field set to review names its reviewer principals here (review 5, A13). RFC 0037 F3 is paid in part here: W7's first half — every key is one of the fifteen policy keys — is now structural, and a named-but-empty principal list is rejected. W7's second half, that every field whose verb is `review` carries a non-empty list, stays a checker rule: JSON Schema cannot quantify a relation between the keys of one object and the values of another, so expressing it needs fifteen hand-written conditionals, which is more machinery than the rule is worth while `policy` and `policy_reviewers` are both in the identity preimage and checked together at acceptance.

additionalProperties.description: Principals whose review satisfies the `review` verb for this field. A `review` verb naming no reviewer is an unenforceable block (W7), so an empty list is rejected.

policy_reviewers.description: Map from policy field name to the principals whose review satisfies the review verb for that field. Keys are the fifteen policy keys and nothing else (W7); the map is inside the `in_*` identity preimage (ID2), so changing a reviewer list mints a new contract.

policy.$comment: RFC 0037 F4, paid here. One enum applied to all fifteen keys let any verb validate on any field, so the W6 applicability matrix was prose: `no-decrease` on `properties` or `no-downgrade` outside `assurance` were schema-valid and had to be rejected by a checker. The per-field restrictions make an inapplicable verb unrepresentable, which is what W6 asks for — an inapplicable verb is rejected, never silently read as `unlocked`.
policy.description: The fifteen protected-field policy verbs (plan §5.4). Each key carries the verbs the RFC 0037 W6 matrix declares admissible for it: a directional verb is well-formed only where the relation it denies is admissible for that field and denying it is the protective direction.

schema_id.description: Artifact-class identity of the governing schema: its `$id` with the `v<schema_epoch>/` segment removed (schemas/README.md). Stable across schema epochs.

schema_epoch.description: Schema epoch this instance was written against (schemas/README.md). It advances only on a breaking change to this artifact class, is not one of the six independently versioned epochs (RFC 0026 `rule versioning.epoch_independence`), and pins no semantics.

security_policy.description: First-class security policy group (plan §5.2): data classification, redaction classes, and capability requirements.

capability_requirements.description: Capabilities required to exercise the operations this intent governs (e.g. revise-intent).

redaction_classes.description: Artifact classes subject to redaction/purge semantics (plan §4.5).

fragments.$comment: RFC 0037 F5 and F11, paid here. Without `minItems` an empty declaration made every unit `unsupported` and every promotion blocked — fail-closed, but silently — where W3 requires `scope.fragments` to be non-empty; and the description wrote the wire literal in prose case, where RFC 0031's relation token is lowercase `unknown` (RFC 0037 correction 1).
fragments.description: Declared semantic fragments (ADR-0025); non-empty per W3. Intent-diff guarantees apply within declared fragments; a unit outside them classifies `unsupported`, and a relation the classifier cannot establish classifies `unknown` — both fail closed (plan §5.3, RFC 0031). Narrowing this set cannot convert a blocked change into an allowed one: it forces re-classification of every unit stated in a removed fragment, and those units then classify `unsupported`.

x-policy-field-map.$comment: Normative map from policy keys to the contract field groups they govern (review 5, A13): policy vocabulary, field vocabulary, and semantic-diff field vocabulary are unified through this table.
